about: Documented exceptions to the insight diagram rule (docs/site/insight-publishing-contract.md, check 11). An inline <svg> diagram in an insight article body must reuse a primitive from site/assets/css/diagrams.css or be listed here, keyed by the page slug and the diagram's exact aria-label. Baseline of 45 recorded on 2026-11-13 (Phase 3b, MnemeHQ/mnemehq-site#302). Patterns carry their consolidation priority; delete an entry when its diagram moves to a primitive.

checkpoints.note: Redraws the canonical enforcement checkpoints diagram: governance firing at successive points from session start to CI. The primitive is fixed at five steps under a two and three split, and two of these pages list six. Migrate once its row takes a variable number of steps.

linear-flow.note: Three to five labelled boxes joined by arrows and read in order. This is the checkpoints row without its brackets or gate, so one variable-step row could serve both. Decide between generalising that row and adding a neutral flow primitive.

layer-stack.note: Bands stacked vertically, one per layer, placing governance or verification relative to the rest. No primitive yet. Two pages draw nearly the same six-layer AI stack (html-is-not-the-point-structure-is and why-context-alone-doesnt-prevent-architectural-drift).

two-panel.note: Two panels side by side, each a heading over a short list, contrasting two things or drawing an analogy. The most uniform cluster; one two-column primitive would cover it.

before-after.note: Two lanes, an old model against a new one, each a short flow. The strategic diagram kept on /concepts/governance-before-generation/ in Phase 3 has the same shape, so a primitive would serve concept pages too.

hub-spoke.note: A central node with surfaces or functions around it. Two instances; keep as exceptions unless it recurs.

diverging-curves.note: Two schematic curves that separate as AI use grows, with the gap labelled. Two instances; keep as exceptions unless it recurs.

bespoke.note: Specific to one article's argument or data. No canonical primitive covers it and no other page draws it; each rationale says why.

exceptions.label: Two diverging curves: AI generation throughput rises steeply while control capacity stays nearly flat. The shaded region between them is the governance gap.
exceptions.rationale: Schematic curves for generation throughput and control capacity with the gap shaded. No primitive draws curves.

exceptions.label: Audit, encode, enforce, verify migration control loop
exceptions.rationale: Four-step migration control loop: audit, encode, enforce, verify. Waits on a flow primitive.

exceptions.label: Two markets: runtime governance protects systems from agent actions; architectural governance protects systems from architectural entropy
exceptions.rationale: Runtime governance and architectural governance as two lists side by side. Waits on a two-panel primitive.

exceptions.label: Enterprises need both: architectural governance over time and runtime governance per action, around autonomous systems
exceptions.rationale: Architectural governance above, runtime governance below, autonomous agents between. Waits on a layer-stack primitive.

exceptions.label: A multi-agent pipeline where the database agent violates an ADR while orchestration reports success
exceptions.rationale: Four-agent pipeline where the database agent breaks an ADR while orchestration reports success. Needs a flow primitive that can mark a failed step.

exceptions.label: The four migration states and how enforcement resolves between them
exceptions.rationale: The four migration states and how path applicability resolves a rule per path. Specific to the migration argument.

exceptions.label: More developers required more management; more agents require more governance
exceptions.rationale: Developers needing management set beside agents needing governance, as an analogy. Waits on a two-panel primitive.

exceptions.label: Productivity gains absorbed by verification overhead
exceptions.rationale: Causal chain from faster generation through review and drift to a muted P&L impact. Waits on a flow primitive.

exceptions.label: The coordination layer sits between orchestration and execution
exceptions.rationale: Coordination infrastructure placed between orchestration and execution, with observability below. Waits on a layer-stack primitive.

exceptions.label: Diagram showing five AI coding tools each with their own memory format, all writing into one shared codebase
exceptions.rationale: A table of five AI coding tools, each with its own memory format, all writing to one codebase. Tabular content no primitive renders.

exceptions.label: Timeline showing four categories — containers, tracing, IDE language servers, AI coding agents — moving through phases of fragmentation, convergence, standard, and adoption
exceptions.rationale: Timeline of containers, tracing, language servers and AI coding agents moving from fragmentation to adoption. Historical data specific to the article.

exceptions.label: Without persistent governance, a decision passes through agent context and compaction before being lost, producing a violation
exceptions.rationale: A decision lost through agent context and compaction, ending in a violation. First of a before/after pair of flows.

exceptions.label: With governance, decisions persist in a store, are retrieved per change, and proposed actions are checked deterministically
exceptions.rationale: The same decision kept in a store, retrieved per change and checked. Second of the pair; waits on a flow primitive.

exceptions.label: Agent changes reaching commits without a manual diff acceptance step rose from 7 percent in January 2026 to 36.3 percent in May 2026
exceptions.rationale: Plots the report's figures, 7 percent in January 2026 to 36.3 percent in May 2026. A schematic primitive would drop the data.

exceptions.label: Governance must apply across six automated surfaces: before generation, before tool execution, before commit, before the PR, in CI, and across generated artifacts
exceptions.rationale: Six governance surfaces from before generation to generated artifacts. Six steps; the checkpoints primitive takes five.

exceptions.label: Tool call evaluated against an external decision corpus at the pre-execute seam, then a verdict, then execution
exceptions.rationale: A tool call checked against the decision corpus at the pre-execute seam, then a verdict, then execution. Waits on a flow primitive.

exceptions.label: Delivery metrics stay green while ungoverned architectural integrity declines as agent velocity rises
exceptions.rationale: Delivery metrics stay healthy while ungoverned architectural integrity declines. Schematic curves; no primitive draws curves.

exceptions.label: The three-layer model of AI software engineering metrics: activity, delivery, governance
exceptions.rationale: Activity, delivery and governance metrics as three layers. Waits on a layer-stack primitive.

exceptions.label: Two questions determine the four protection states: how much of the decision can be represented deterministically, and whether that rule already exists
exceptions.rationale: Two questions that cross into four protection states. A decision diagram unique to this article.

exceptions.label: Two axes: GitHub's Trust Layer grades the run's behavior probabilistically; architectural conformance decides the diff against ratified decisions deterministically
exceptions.rationale: GitHub's Trust Layer grading the run set beside architectural conformance deciding the diff. Waits on a two-panel primitive.

exceptions.label: Two orthogonal axes: a registry governs the actor by identity and authorization; architectural governance returns a verdict on the artifact by intent and conformance
exceptions.rationale: A registry governing the actor set beside architectural governance judging the artifact. Waits on a two-panel primitive.

exceptions.label: The shift from calling a model to calling a managed agent runtime
exceptions.rationale: A model call, the old pattern, against a managed agent runtime, the new one. Waits on a before/after primitive.

exceptions.label: Execution is provider-operated; governance is owned by you
exceptions.rationale: Provider-operated execution set beside governance the customer owns. Waits on a two-panel primitive.

exceptions.label: Old vs new governance perimeter
exceptions.rationale: The centralized governance perimeter against the new endpoint perimeter. Waits on a before/after primitive.

exceptions.label: The expanding agent execution surface
exceptions.rationale: The agent execution surface at the centre with seven surfaces around it. One of two hub-and-spoke diagrams.

exceptions.label: Reliability asks whether a run completed; verification asks whether it stayed correct and compliant
exceptions.rationale: Reliability, whether a run completed, set beside verification, whether it stayed correct. Waits on a two-panel primitive.

exceptions.label: From documents to executable environments
exceptions.rationale: Progression from raw text to executable environments. Waits on a flow primitive.

exceptions.label: The AI stack and where governance engineering sits
exceptions.rationale: Six-layer AI stack with governance engineering placed in it. Nearly the same stack as why-context-alone-doesnt-prevent-architectural-drift; consolidate the two.

exceptions.label: Diagram showing a long-running agent session flow with both continuity infrastructure and governance checkpoints
exceptions.rationale: A long agent session drawn as two tracks, continuity artifacts and governance checkpoints. Specific to this article.

exceptions.label: Diagram showing five governance checkpoint positions in the agent workflow
exceptions.rationale: Five checkpoints, each with an enforcement mode and what it catches. Fits the five-step row, but each step carries a line more detail than the primitive holds.

exceptions.label: Diagram comparing the optimization target of memory systems (recall) against governance systems (constraint enforcement)
exceptions.rationale: One query through a memory system and a governance system, contrasting recall with enforcement. A three-column comparison specific to the argument.

exceptions.label: Stack diagram showing memory, context, and retrieval as inputs that flow into a governance layer that produces a single enforced constraint
exceptions.rationale: Memory, retrieval, context and scope signals feeding a governance layer that emits one constraint. A fan-in specific to the argument.

exceptions.label: Old vs new PR review model
exceptions.rationale: Collaborative PR review, the old model, against containment review under agent velocity. Waits on a before/after primitive.

exceptions.label: Moving governance upstream of PR review
exceptions.rationale: Five steps that move enforcement upstream of PR review. Fits the five-step row; its closing line would move into the caption.

exceptions.label: Prompt engineering optimizes a single input to the model; harness engineering designs the runtime system loop around the model
exceptions.rationale: A single prompt-to-output path against the harness loop around the model. Waits on a before/after primitive.

exceptions.label: The six-layer agent infrastructure stack
exceptions.rationale: Six-layer agent infrastructure stack, L1 to L6. Waits on a layer-stack primitive.

exceptions.label: Architectural decisions feed Mneme, which constrains IBM Bob before implementation
exceptions.rationale: ADRs through guardrails to IBM Bob to a compliant implementation. Waits on a flow primitive.

exceptions.label: Three layers of physical agent guardrails
exceptions.rationale: Three layers of physical agent guardrails, from human policy to device limits. Waits on a layer-stack primitive.

exceptions.label: An agent harness is the execution layer around the model, coordinating tool calls, retries, context and state, routing, and multi-step execution
exceptions.rationale: The harness around the model, coordinating tool calls, retries, context, routing and multi-step runs. One of two hub-and-spoke diagrams.

exceptions.label: The execution stack: generation produces, orchestration (the harness) executes, governance decides what is allowed
exceptions.rationale: Generation, orchestration and governance as a three-layer execution stack. Waits on a layer-stack primitive.

exceptions.label: Diagram showing two overlapping ADRs producing non-deterministic resolution across prompt rules, RAG, and PR review, versus deterministic resolution via a precedence engine
exceptions.rationale: Two overlapping ADRs resolved inconsistently by prompt rules, RAG and review, against a precedence engine. Specific to the precedence argument.

exceptions.label: Pipeline showing five stages from raw ADRs to enforcement and audit, with precedence resolution as the central stage
exceptions.rationale: Five numbered stages from raw ADRs to enforcement and audit, with precedence at the centre. Waits on a flow primitive with step numbers.

exceptions.label: Layer progression from prompting to verification
exceptions.rationale: Six layers from prompting to verification. Nearly the same stack as html-is-not-the-point-structure-is; consolidate the two.

exceptions.label: How drift emerges through agent execution
exceptions.rationale: How drift enters: retrieved context, execution, local optimization, deviation, then review. Waits on a flow primitive.

exceptions.label: Governance insertion points across the development workflow
exceptions.rationale: Six governance insertion points from session start to runtime verification. Six steps; the checkpoints primitive takes five. Overlaps cursor-developer-habits-report-governance-infrastructure.
